text:
Alex: quick sync re: admission tokens and cost attribution for dedicated pool pre-warms. we've seen noisy tenant churn in the billing reports when operator issues short-lived reservations.
Priya: saw that alert. looks like many tiny reservations (~5-30s) inflate metering records. do we want operator to collapse short leases into a single billing grain?
Hugo: problem is we currently bill by reservation start events. if accept/release happens fast, we still count full reservation unit which skews cost.
Lina: proposal: introduce an admission_token lifecycle with fields: token_id, requested_capacity, lease_hint_s, billing_grain_s. operator can return a token with billed_s which <= actual_held_s and we'll bill that amount.
Alex: so operator returns billed_s to avoid double-counting transient holds? good. but need anti-abuse: ensure billed_s >= min_bill_window (config).
Priya: min_bill_window default 15s. operator can aggregate multiple small tokens from same tenant into one billed interval if they overlap.
Hugo: acceptance API sketch: POST /v1/admit -> {token_id, tenant, capacity, lease_hint_s}. operator responds 200 {reservation_token, accepted_capacity, billed_s, ready_eta_s}. idempotent on token_id.
Lina: also add a OPT_OUT_BILLING flag for internal test tenants so we can canary without cost noise.
Grace: telemetry ask: emit metric admission_token_lifecycle{phase="issued|accepted|released|billed", tenant, pool}. want percentiles of held_s and billed_s.
Alex: edge case: operator delays longer than lease_hint_s. how does autoscaler react? two options: extend lease, or consider rejected and fall back to reactive warmup. thoughts?
Priya: prefer fallback + cooldown. extending leases silently masks operator slowness. fallback triggers reactive warmup and marks the original token as stale. operator then can accept but must signal "stale_accept" so autoscaler ignores it.
Hugo: need a clear race-safe flow: 1) forecast emits token T1 with lease_hint 30s. 2) operator takes 40s to provision. 3) autoscaler should have started reactive prewarm at ~30s. operator must attach stale=true when finally accepting T1. 4) if operator still provisions, we can reconcile and credit billed_s to tenant but not double-run prewarm.
Lina: to avoid double-run we can include a prewarm_id in the accept response which maps to active prewarm action. autoscaler will check for existing prewarm_id before launching reactive job.
Grace: add metric prewarm_duplicate_detected{tenant} when autoscaler finds active prewarm_id and cancels its own. helps measure race frequency.
Alex: security: token must be signed HMAC by forecast service. operator verifies signature. token_id uniq per forecast event.
Priya: rollout: implement token schema + idempotent accept endpoint -> canary 5 tenants -> enable billed_s reporting in billing pipeline -> 4 week canary analyzing billing skew -> widen. Lina will draft rollout steps.
Hugo: one more: reservation granularity. do we reserve in gpu-slots or fractional GPUs? fractional is great for cost but operator needs packing hints. include shape_hint (e.g., {cpu:2,mem_gb:6,gpu_frac:0.25}) in token.
Lina: packing hint should be advisory only. operator can override accepted_capacity and include accepted_shape. must surface accepted_shape in traces.
Grace: queries for dashboards: 1) rate(admission_token_issued[5m]) by tenant 2) histogram(admission_token_held_s) 3) sum(billed_s) / sum(held_s) to see efficiency.
Alex: ok action items: Lina draft API + token schema PR, Priya wire HMAC signing in forecast svc, Hugo add billing adapter stub, Grace add dashboards/alerts, I'll own rollout checklist and coordination with billing.
orch-bot: noted. will post canary report when admission_token_issued > 100 for canary tenants.
Priya: thanks 44d let's reconvene after Lina's API PR is in.
Lina: will post draft in ~2 hours.
Hugo: i'll stub the billing adapter today.
Grace: dashboard PR in the afternoon.
Alex: excellent. keeping the token minimal and lease-driven should help reduce double-billing and make operator-autoscaler handoff explicit.
